subject: tu:game/world/gauntworld
value:
BOUNDARY ON claim.law.IH_multiset-gain-does-not-imply-fuzzy-gain-arbitrate-with-count-distance.20260901.v1. That law is right that instruction-count distance is the best cheap predictor of fuzzy, and its four measurements stand. But its operational rule - 'when both improve, expect a win' - HAS A COUNTEREXAMPLE, and the counterexample is not marginal: ALL THREE cheap predictors improved together and fuzzy still LOST.

THE MEASUREMENT, gauntworld fn_8005E90C (270 target instructions), both sides from full green ninja builds with build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK, fuzzy read with tools/gdl/fuzzy.py from the regenerated report:
  real                      158 -> 143   BETTER
  opcode multiset            4t -> 3t    BETTER
  instruction-count distance  2 -> 1     BETTER  (ours 268 -> 269 against target 270)
  objdiff fuzzy         96.1407 -> 95.9815   WORSE
The edit closed an entire structural cluster: a target-only `mr` that had no counterpart in our stream disappeared from the --ops multiset outright.

WHY IT HAPPENS, and this is the part the count-distance proxy cannot see. objdiff's score is alignment-sensitive at CLUSTER granularity, not just at length granularity. Before the edit, the missing `mr` and an adjacent pair of `lwz` argument loads emitted in the opposite order were absorbed into ONE diff cluster. Closing the `mr` did not fix the `lwz` order, and the surviving disagreement SPLIT INTO TWO separately-aligned clusters. Fuzzy charged for the extra cluster boundary by more than it credited the recovered instruction. So the real predictor of a fuzzy loss is a rise in the number of distinct aligned clusters, which neither count distance nor the multiset token count reports.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE. Count distance remains the right cheap screen for whether to SPEND an arbitration build - it is free from probe.py's banner and it was right in four of five measured cases across two lanes. It is NOT a substitute for the build, and 'all cheap predictors agree' does not license skipping it. When a fix closes one of several mechanisms sharing a diff cluster, budget for the arbitration build specifically, and read the --ops CLUSTER COUNT before and after, not only the multiset line.

ARBITRATION PRECEDENT SET HERE, for the next agent who hits this. The change was RETAINED despite the fuzzy loss, on these grounds together: AGENTS.md makes `real` the arbiter below roughly 4000 instructions and this function is 270; the --ops diff was actually read and shows a genuine structural cluster closed rather than reshuffled; defake_gate returned GATE OK with no regression among the TU's 33 real-0 functions; and project-level progress was unchanged at reporting resolution (Game Code 97.88% fuzzy / 55.95% matched before and after), so the loss does not reach the project metric at all. A fuzzy dip that is invisible at project resolution and buys a closed structural mechanism is progress toward EXACT, which is the mandated product; a fuzzy dip with no structural gain is not. State the conflict in the commit and the record either way - this one is committed as 'Reconstruct fn_8005E90C (158 -> 143 real diffs)' precisely so it does not read as a fuzzy improvement.

MEASUREMENT HYGIENE NOTE, cost one wasted reading. The same source state read 95.9407 once and 95.9815 on two subsequent consecutive full builds. The 95.9407 was taken from a report produced in the same invocation sequence as a defake_gate --rebuild plus --update-improved; the stable value is 95.9815. Read fuzzy from a report generated by a PLAIN full ninja that has settled, and confirm any number you are about to record by reading it twice - AGENTS.md discipline 8 (write records FROM tool output) does not protect you if the tool output itself is taken mid-sequence.
